summary: Two deliverables. (A) TOOLING ROOT CAUSE: the committed maze .state.gz fixtures CANNOT unserialize on the patched trace core — root-caused precisely to a per-build serialize-layout divergence in DBPSerialize_CPU (the inter-function offset checkpoint fails at switch ln=313). The two cores EMULATE IDENTICALLY (the nightly core renders all 3 committed maze .idx.gz oracles 0-pixel-exact) but do NOT round-trip serialize-states. A fresh patched-core drive cannot reproduce the committed frame (lands at party cell x=3, committed is x=5 — x=5 is not reachable by walking forward from a fresh dungeon entry, the party starts at x=2 and a wall blocks at x=3), so re-minting WOULD change the .idx.gz — which the task forbids and which is NOT warranted (the renderers agree; only driving/positioning + serialize-blob diverge). Therefore the .idx.gz oracles are LEFT UNCHANGED, the committed states are LEFT UNCHANGED, and the harness default core is RESTORED to nightly. The patched core remains the page-capture tool, driven via trace-maze.ts reach (fresh CLEAN_STATE) — which it CAN serialize/capture; page-capture does NOT depend on the committed states. (B) PIECE INVENTORY: captured + 100%/100%-decoded a full maze compose-page on the freshly-built patched core (corridor-at-gate view: ceiling/floor/side-walls + central green portcullis window). Cross-referenced the wall_emit_quad shape jump-table + the two-compositor architecture (masked wall writer + floor/ceiling OR-blit) from maze-stage1-compositor.json. The finite finish-line checklist is below.

findings.claim: The committed maze states (test-fixtures/states/maze-corridor.state.gz, 613923 B raw) fail to unserialize on the patched trace core with 'Load State Error: Invalid file format' (DBPArchive::ERR_LAYOUT). Both cores write serialize version 8, magic 0xD05B5747, and BYTE-IDENTICAL config headers (machine=0x05 memory=0x10 vgamem=0x10) — so the header check passes. The failure is the per-function offset checkpoint (dbp_serialize.cpp line 357: `ar << off; if (off != offcheck) ERR_LAYOUT`), which fires at switch ln=313 = DBPSerialize_CPU. The nightly buildbot core (fetch-core.sh) and our pinned-commit patched core (build-core.sh @ 42485508) — though origin/main HEAD == the pin, same osx arm64 build, same C_DYNREC=1 — emit a DIFFERENT serialized byte-count for the CPU block, so version-8 blobs are NOT cross-compatible between the two builds. The trace patch itself is NOT the cause (it adds only non-serialized static buffers + a MIXER_CallBack len<=0 guard; touches core_normal.cpp / mixer.cpp / paging.h, none of which are in the serialize path).

evidence.details: Probe (unserialize committed state on each core): patched core -> 'err unser' / log 'Load State Error: Invalid file format'; nightly core -> OK, re-serializes to exactly 613923 B, and renders maze-corridor / maze-corridor-turn-left / maze-corridor-lookback ALL 0 differing px vs the committed .idx.gz oracles (palette-misses 0). Temporary stderr instrumentation at dbp_serialize.cpp:357 logged '[WIZ6-SERDIAG] LAYOUT mismatch at func ln=313: read-offset=<garbage> checkpoint=525' — ln=313 = DBPSerialize_CPU in the __LINE__ switch (cpu.cpp DBPSerialize_CPU). Config-header bytes decoded identical on both cores. Diagnostic reverted; cores rebuilt clean.

findings.claim: The two cores RENDER IDENTICALLY — this is NOT the 'cores diverge' case the task warns about. The nightly core reproduces every committed maze .idx.gz oracle pixel-exact (0 diff). The patched core decodes a freshly-captured compose-page to 100.00% viewport + 100.00% chrome vs its OWN same-frame framebuffer (re-confirmed this run for two views). The mismatch is ONLY in (1) the serialize blob layout (DBPSerialize_CPU, above) and (2) the fresh-drive landing cell. So the .idx.gz oracles are CORRECT and were left untouched; no re-mint was performed.

findings.claim: A fresh patched-core drive (trace-maze driveToMaze / the MAZE_CORRIDOR recipe) lands at party cell x=3 gy=119, NOT the committed x=5 gy=121. Walking forward from a fresh dungeon entry, the party starts at x=2 and can only advance to x=3 (a wall blocks further forward). So the committed corridor frame (x=5) is NOT reachable by the current forward-walk recipe on the patched core — the committed state encodes a position the fresh drive does not reach. Re-minting the .state on the patched core would therefore render a DIFFERENT viewport (corridor histogram {0:3994,1:1198,8:5796,9:8304,...} vs committed {0:4005,1:743,8:6698,9:8179,...}; whole-viewport divergence ~9000-25000 px, not a few animation pixels) and change the .idx.gz. Per the task caveat, STOP + report rather than re-mint: the divergence is in DRIVING, not RENDERING.
